jurisdiction.name: Los Angeles
jurisdiction.notes: City of Los Angeles only; Santa Monica, West Hollywood, Beverly Hills, Pasadena, Long Beach and Culver City are separate cities with their own permits (and Pasadena, Long Beach and Vernon have their own health departments). Health permits come from LA County Public Health; most other approvals route through LADBS's Clearance Summary Worksheet.

permits.name: Business Tax Registration Certificate (BTRC)
permits.issuing_agency: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance
permits.notes: Every business operating in the City of Los Angeles must register; registering online gives you a temporary certificate or registration number immediately and the permanent BTRC arrives by mail in 4–6 weeks. There is usually nothing to pay up front: first-year business tax is billed as 'back tax' when you renew in year two, and businesses with under $100,000 in gross receipts that renew on time qualify for the Small Business Exemption (some classifications owe a minimum payment at registration). The online application also flags whether you need Police, Fire or Tobacco permits, which are billed through the same account.

permits.name: Fictitious Business Name (DBA) statement – Los Angeles County
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk
permits.notes: Needed when you trade under a name other than the owner's surname or the exact entity name. The first-time filing fee is $26 for one name and one registrant; within 45 days of filing you must publish the statement once a week for four consecutive weeks in an adjudicated LA County newspaper (prices range from about $29 to several hundred dollars, so shop around). Banks, ABC and the BTRC application ask for it.

permits.name: Retail food facility plan check (new construction / remodel)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles County Dept. of Public Health – Environmental Health, Plan Check Program
permits.notes: Required before building any new or remodeled food facility in LA County (except in Pasadena, Long Beach and Vernon, which run their own health departments). FY2026–27 restaurant plan check fees run $1,044 (≤500 sq ft) to $2,723 (10,000+ sq ft); the fee covers two plan reviews and two field inspections, with extra work billed at $167/hr. Initial review is promised within 20 business days of payment (10 business days with the expedited fee, $1,566–$4,085), but most projects need at least one correction cycle, so budget 1–2.5 months.
permits.stall_risk: Correction cycles on equipment cut sheets, finish schedules and hood/ventilation details routinely add 3–6 weeks, and LADBS will not issue the building permit until Health signs its clearance. Submit complete plans with a food-experienced designer, or pay the expedite fee if the lease clock is running.

permits.name: Public Health Permit/License to operate a food facility
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles County Dept. of Public Health – Environmental Health
permits.notes: For new construction or remodels, the plan checker hands you the permit application at the final construction inspection; for a change of ownership of an existing restaurant you request an inspection from the district office instead. Do not pay until DPH invoices you. FY2026–27 annual restaurant fees range from $319 (0–30 seats, low risk) to $1,438 (151+ seats, high risk), and the facility must have a certified food protection manager on staff at the inspection.
permits.stall_risk: Failed final inspections (missing hand-wash or mop sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water, missing manager certificate) push openings by 1–3 weeks. Walk the space against the retail construction guideline before calling for the final.

permits.name: LADBS building permit (tenant improvements / change of use)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)
permits.notes: Kitchen build-outs, hoods, restrooms, ADA upgrades and any change of use need plans filed and approved by LADBS before a permit is issued; simple scopes can go through counter or expanded-counter plan check, larger ones through regular plan check on ePlanLA. Fees scale with valuation (plan check is roughly 80% of the permit fee). LADBS issues a Clearance Summary Worksheet listing sign-offs from County Health, LA Sanitation (grease), LAFD and City Planning (alcohol conditions) that must be cleared before issuance. Ask for a case manager from the free Restaurant & Small Business Express Program as soon as design is done.
permits.stall_risk: Clearance items from other departments (Health, LASAN FOG, LAFD, Planning) are what usually hold up issuance, not the LADBS review itself. Enroll in the Restaurant & Small Business Express Program and chase each clearance in parallel.

permits.name: Certificate of Occupancy (change of use / new building)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)
permits.notes: A Certificate of Occupancy is required for new buildings and for any change of use or occupancy (e.g. retail to restaurant); a plain tenant improvement within the same use does not get a new CofO. It is issued when all permit inspections and agency clearances are signed off, and a Temporary CofO can be purchased to open while minor items are finished. Pull the existing CofO and permit history first: parking counts and occupant load on record often dictate whether the change of use is feasible.

permits.name: LAFD fire/life safety plan review (hood suppression, alarms, change of use)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles Fire Department – Fire Development Services
permits.notes: LAFD fire protection engineers review new construction, change-of-use and remodel plans for State Fire Marshal occupancies, including assembly (A-2) restaurants and bars, fire alarm systems and kitchen hood suppression; submittals go through the FIMS portal with site, floor and roof plans. LAFD sign-off is one of the clearances on the LADBS Clearance Summary Worksheet. Fees depend on scope and system type.

permits.name: LAFD annual fire permit – A-2 food/drink assemblage (50+ occupants)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles Fire Department (billed by the Office of Finance)
permits.notes: Restaurants, bars and clubs with an occupant load of 50 or more are A-2 assembly occupancies and need an annual LAFD fire permit, billed through your Office of Finance account (rates effective 9/13/2025: $764 for 50–99 occupants, $1,146 for 100–499, $1,528 for 500+). The LAFD Public Assemblage Unit sets and enforces posted occupancy limits and inspects exits. Candles, open flame and temporary cooking need separate LAFD special permits.

permits.name: Conditional Use Permit for alcohol (CUB)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles City Planning – Beverage and Entertainment Streamlining (BESt) Unit / Office of Zoning Administration
permits.notes: Any on-site alcohol sales to the public in LA need City Planning authorization; bars, hotels, late-night restaurants and anything that does not qualify for the Restaurant Beverage Program need a stand-alone CUB. File by appointment with the BESt Unit, then a project planner prepares a public hearing before a Zoning Administrator, who issues a Letter of Determination with conditions (hours, security, noise) followed by an appeal period. City Planning says the normal CUB takes at least six months; fees were raised effective February 23, 2026 and include monitoring and inspection (MViP) fees at condition clearance. ABC will not issue the license until the CUB is effectuated.
permits.stall_risk: The CUB hearing is the critical path for any LA bar: 6–12 months with neighborhood council review, possible appeals, and conditions that may cap hours. File as soon as the lease is signed (with a CUB contingency) and meet the neighborhood council and LAPD vice before the hearing.

permits.name: Restaurant Beverage Program (RBP) administrative alcohol authorization
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles City Planning – Beverage and Entertainment Streamlining (BESt) Unit
permits.notes: Streamlined alternative to the CUB for sit-down restaurants in Council-designated RBP-eligible areas (check ZIMAS) that agree to 50+ operating standards: hours limited to 7 am–11 pm, a full menu with continuous food service, no cover charge or age restrictions, and alcohol served by staff. City Planning's fact sheet quotes about one month to authorization and a total cost of $5,910.15 including monitoring and two inspections (2026 fee update may raise this). Apply through Planning's Online Application System with the floor plan, menu and Certificate of Occupancy; three violations in two years disqualifies the restaurant for five years.

permits.name: Conditional Use Permit for public dancing / entertainment (CUX)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles City Planning – BESt Unit / Office of Zoning Administration
permits.notes: Patron dancing in a bar, club or restaurant requires a CUX, filed with the BESt Unit and heard by a Zoning Administrator (usually alongside the CUB in a single case). LAPD will not grant a Dance Hall permit at a location that has never held one until this zoning approval exists; hotels, catering halls and schools are exempt. Expect conditions on hours, security staffing and sound.

permits.name: Police Commission Café Entertainment & Shows permit (live music / performers)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles Police Commission – Commission Investigation Division, Permit Processing Section
permits.notes: Businesses offering live entertainment or shows (bands, DJs, comedy, karaoke) need a Café Entertainment police permit. Email the Permit Processing Section for the packet, submit it, pay through the Office of Finance ($1,118 original fee, $393 annual renewal), then an investigator inspects, may issue a temporary permit, and the Police Permit Review Panel decides; a grant letter is valid 90 days until the permit arrives. Owners undergo background checks, nearby neighborhood councils are notified, and permits are not transferable to a new owner.

permits.name: Police Commission Dance Hall permit
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles Police Commission – Commission Investigation Division
permits.notes: Any location where the public is invited to dance needs a Dance Hall permit (LAMC 103.106); it also covers live bands playing for dancing, so no separate live-entertainment permit is needed for them. All legal owners apply with entity documents, the lease, an LADBS zoning referral slip and the current ABC license; the site is posted for 21 days and the notice published twice in a local paper. Fees are $667 original and $393 annual.
permits.stall_risk: A first-time dance location must have a CUX from City Planning before LAPD will process the permit, and the 21-day protest period invites neighbor objections. Sequence CUX, then ABC, then the police permit, and budget 9–15 months in total.

permits.name: Industrial Wastewater Permit for food service establishments (FOG / grease interceptor)
permits.issuing_agency: LA Sanitation & Environment (LASAN) – Industrial Waste Management Division
permits.notes: Under LAMC 64.30 every food service establishment that generates grease must hold an Industrial Wastewater Permit, follow kitchen best management practices and run an approved gravity or hydromechanical grease interceptor; new construction and remodels valued at $100,000+ must install one. The permit carries an application fee at submittal plus recurring inspection-and-control fees (LASAN does not post current amounts; historically about $600 to apply plus roughly $430 a year). The IWMD clearance appears on the LADBS Clearance Summary Worksheet and is booked through the City's One-Stop appointment portal.
permits.stall_risk: Interceptor sizing disputes and the lack of exterior space for a gravity interceptor are a classic LA build-out delay; finding out at plan check can force a redesign. Get the IWMD sizing determination during schematic design.

permits.name: Sign permit (exterior business signage)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)
permits.notes: New or replaced exterior signs need their own LADBS application separate from the building permit, and illuminated signs also need an electrical permit. Sign size and type are limited by the zoning code and any specific plan or sign district, which can require City Planning sign-off. Fees follow the LADBS fee schedule based on sign type and valuation.

permits.name: LA Al Fresco sidewalk dining (Revocable Permit) and outdoor alcohol authorization
permits.issuing_agency: City of Los Angeles – Bureau of Engineering (Revocable Permit), LAFD, City Planning
permits.notes: The permanent Al Fresco ordinance lets restaurants use sidewalks, parking lanes and private lots for dining. Sidewalk dining needs a Bureau of Engineering Revocable Permit ($215 limited service / $556 full service), a one-time Sewer Facilities Charge per added seat ($138 / $165), a $504 LAFD inspection and plot-plan review, a waiver of damages and liability insurance; on-street dining adds a $1,200–$1,500 application review fee (fees as of January 1, 2026). Serving alcohol outdoors also needs an Al Fresco Alcohol Authorization from City Planning on top of your CUB or RBP.

permits.name: Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) Registration Certificate
permits.issuing_agency: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance
permits.notes: Any operator renting rooms for stays of 30 days or less must obtain a TOT Registration Certificate within 30 days of starting operations and collect the 14% TOT. Returns and payment are monthly: due the first of the following month, delinquent after the 25th. Keep signed agreements for exempt 30+ day stays and government guests for at least three years.

permits.name: Police Commission hotel permit (Responsible Hotel Ordinance)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles Police Commission – Hotels and Short-Term Rentals Section
permits.notes: Since July 1, 2024, Ordinance 188072 (LAMC Chapter X, Division 10) requires hotels, motels, hostels and apartment hotels in the City to obtain a Police Commission permit; applications are emailed to hotels@lapd.online along with the RHO compliance registration. LAPD told the City Council in 2024 it lacked staff to implement the program, so processing times and fees are still unsettled; confirm the current fee with the section before budgeting. Separately, new hotel developments need City Planning approval under the same ordinance.

permits.name: Mobile Food Facility health permit and plan check (truck / cart)
permits.issuing_agency: Los Angeles County Dept. of Public Health – Environmental Health
permits.notes: Trucks and carts must pass a mobile food facility plan check ($544–$741 in FY2026–27) and then hold an annual health permit ($325 low risk to $761 high risk; compact carts $126–$592) tied to an approved commissary. LA County does not cover Pasadena, Long Beach or Vernon, which require their own permits. Fee structures were overhauled in March 2024 to lower costs for sidewalk vendors.

permits.name: Sidewalk & Park Vending Permit (carts and stands)
permits.issuing_agency: City of Los Angeles – StreetsLA (Bureau of Street Services)
permits.notes: Anyone selling food or merchandise from a cart or stand on City sidewalks or in City parks needs this permit, renewed every 12 months; you must already have a BTRC, a seller's permit and (for food) the County health permit. Apply by appointment at StreetsLA (Downtown or Van Nuys) or by calling 213-847-6000. The City has cut the fee sharply and a 2026 City/County cart program offers free carts and fee waivers to low-income vendors; motorized food trucks parked at the curb do not use this permit but must follow LAMC parking and distance rules.
